finding.title: Move TutorAuditLogReadRepository/TutorGrantRepository interfaces into domain/repositories/ to remove the data→presentation import
finding.rule: Placement guide ("New repository interface → domain/repositories/") / layering
finding.why: coding-standards.md's placement guide says a new repository interface belongs at `domain/repositories/<name>_repository.dart`. None of tutoring's three repository interfaces live there: TutorAuditLogReadRepository is defined inside presentation/providers/audit_log_providers.dart, so the DATA-layer implementation (firestore_audit_log_read_repository.dart) has to import a PRESENTATION file to satisfy `implements` — the exact inverse of the documented data-flow direction — pulling Riverpod Provider definitions and an unrelated stub class into what should be a lean, presentation-agnostic data module and complicating isolated unit-testing of the repository (Feathers seam). TutorGrantRepository is at least kept in domain/ but lives in a use_cases file instead of domain/repositories/, the same underlying placement drift.
finding.recommendation: Create lib/features/tutoring/domain/repositories/tutor_audit_log_repository.dart (read) and tutor_grant_repository.dart, move the three interfaces there, and update data-layer implementations plus presentation/providers imports accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: TutorAuditLogReadRepository, TutorAuditLogRepository, TutorGrantRepository all resolve from lib/features/tutoring/domain/repositories/.

finding.title: Replace source-text-matching and self-asserting tests with real behavioral tests (ws3_3f_manage_remove_tutors_test.dart, firestore_tutor_grant_repository_test.dart)

evidence.quote: const result = TutorGrantFailure(message: message, code: code);

finding.why: ws3_3f_manage_remove_tutors_test.dart never mounts a widget or runs the app — every one of its 8 assertions is `expect(File(...).readAsStringSync(), contains('some_identifier'))` against manage_tutors_screen.dart's own source text. It would pass unchanged even if `_revoke()`/`_rescind()` were completely broken, which they currently are (see the discarded-TutorGrantResult finding). firestore_tutor_grant_repository_test.dart's 'exception mapping' tests construct a TutorGrantFailure literal and then assert it equals the literal they just built ('We verify the mapping contract by replicating the repo logic') — they never call the real repository or its catch blocks. Separately, every mock override of revoke/rescind/resign in manage_tutors_screen_l1_test.dart and manage_grants_screen_l1_test.dart returns only TutorGrantSuccess(); TutorGrantFailure/TutorGrantPreconditionError are never stubbed anywhere in the tutoring widget-test suite. This is precisely the coverage gap that let the P1 discarded-result bug ship.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite ws3_3f_manage_remove_tutors_test.dart's assertions as widget tests that tap Revoke/Rescind and assert the resulting UI state and provider calls; delete or fold firestore_tutor_grant_repository_test.dart's self-asserting exception-mapping tests into the comprehensive test/features/tutoring/data/repositories/firestore_tutor_grant_repository_test.dart, which does exercise the real class via the FirebaseFunctionsPlatform seam.
acceptance_criteria: ws3_3f_manage_remove_tutors_test.dart no longer reads manage_tutors_screen.dart as a string; each test exercises ProviderContainer/widget behavior.
At least one test per revoke/resign/rescind path stubs TutorGrantFailure and asserts the UI does not take the success branch (ties into the P1 finding's acceptance test).

finding.title: Convert TutorPermissions to @freezed instead of hand-writing ==/hashCode
finding.why: coding-standards.md is explicit: domain value objects must be `@freezed` with generated `==`/`hashCode`/`copyWith`, specifically because hand-rolled equality drifts from the field list. TutorPermissions — its own doc-comment calls it 'Immutable value object' / 'VO' — hand-writes both operators across 9 fields, plus a separately hand-written constructor, copyWith, toFirestore, and fromFirestore: 5 places a future field addition must be updated by hand. The drift risk is already visible today: `canMarkLiveCompletion` is deliberately excluded from both `==` and `hashCode` (harmless only because it is hardcoded false for every instance) — exactly the kind of silent omission @freezed generation would make structurally impossible.
finding.recommendation: Convert TutorPermissions to a @freezed class (keeping canMarkLiveCompletion as a computed getter rather than a constructor field, or a private default so it can't be set), and delete the hand-written ==/hashCode/copyWith.
acceptance_criteria: TutorPermissions.freezed.dart is generated; no hand-written operator == or hashCode remains in tutor_permissions.dart.
Existing TutorPermissions unit tests (defaults/readOnly/toFirestore round-trip) still pass unmodified.

finding.title: Handle mid-loop failure in TutoredWriteRouter.pushStageDefinitions (tutored_write_router.dart)
finding.rule: Nygard (partial I/O failure) / DB-6 offline-first parity
finding.why: pushStageDefinitions awaits one Cloud Function call per stage sequentially and _handleResult throws immediately on the first TutorWriteFailure. If a tutor edits several stages at once and the network drops partway through, the earlier stages are already committed server-side while the remaining ones are simply lost — the thrown TutorWriteException names only the failing stage, not which stages already succeeded. Unlike the normal (non-tutored) write path, tutored writes deliberately bypass the local outbox (per this file's own header comment), so there is no retry queue to pick the dropped stages back up on reconnect — the class's offline-first guarantee (DB-6, exercised everywhere else in this app) does not hold here. This is architectural/edge-case reasoning, not a reproduced runtime failure.
finding.recommendation: Either batch the per-stage calls into a single CF invocation (atomic on the server) or collect per-stage results and surface a structured partial-failure summary (which stages succeeded/failed) so the caller can retry just the failed subset instead of losing silent state.
acceptance_criteria: A test that fails the 2nd of 3 stage upserts asserts the caller learns which stages succeeded (not just a single opaque exception).
Documented decision (in tutored_write_router.dart's header) on whether partial multi-stage failure is an accepted risk or gets a retry path.

finding.title: Split the four tutoring screens over the AG-3 400-line cap
finding.why: AG-3 caps hand-written Dart files at 400 lines; these four screens run 411–565, mostly from each _buildXxx step (loading/success/error/confirm) being a full private widget class inlined in the same file. Not a correctness bug, but each screen mixes route-level state machine logic with 4-5 fully-styled sub-widgets, making them slower to review/diff and easy to keep growing.
finding.recommendation: Extract each screen's per-step bodies (_buildReadyToAccept/_buildSuccess/_buildError etc., and the _GrantRow/_TutorGrantRow row widgets) into presentation/widgets/ files.
acceptance_criteria: find lib/features/tutoring -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' returns empty.
